verdict.rationale: Unit's own docs state that deposit and wallet accounts are held in FBO structures. They also say teams get Dashboard and API access to account and transaction data on a native ledger, which partly answers the structure and ledger-visibility parts of the story. Nothing in the evidence says where FDIC insurance attaches, whether pass-through coverage reaches end users, or how FBO pooling compares with individually titled accounts. missing for 10: FDIC insurance attachment/pass-through documentation, explicit FBO-pool vs individual-account explanation, clear rules on who can view the ledger (end users vs platform vs bank), independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a finance lead, the account structure is transparent — whether funds sit in FBO pools or individual accounts, where FDIC insurance actually attaches, and who can see the ledger, all documented plainly

citations.quote: Create deposit accounts and wallet accounts held in FBO structures.
The Unit Dashboard and APIs provide teams with access to customer, account, payment, card, transaction, compliance, and operational data.
They run on a unified infrastructure and native ledger
